comparator.name: Psychology (English)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: a 60-ECTS multidisciplinary first year, a 60-ECTS second year containing 42 ECTS of common psychology, professional and research courses plus 18 ECTS in the selected major, and a third year with a 6-ECTS major practice course, a genuine 30-ECTS mobility window, 12 ECTS of methods and philosophy of science, and a 12-ECTS thesis. Clinical Psychology is the first-listed of nine equally formal majors and is instantiated only as an official-order tie-break. The open mobility window is retained without invented content and zero-credit GROW meetings are excluded.
components: Introduction to Psychology and History of Psychology
Three 6-ECTS Clinical Psychology specialization courses; retained as one official route component because the public curriculum reports the major at category level.
The selected major concludes with one 6-ECTS professional-practice course.
Mobility Window: exchange, Psychology minor and electives
Genuine 30-ECTS mobility or minor-and-elective space; no elective content is invented.

routeSelection.basis: The generic English Psychology target offers nine equally formal majors and does not identify one as the broad default. Clinical Psychology is listed first on the official current programme page, so it is selected as the neutral official-order tie-break before and independently of UCR course selection.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Human thought, emotion, behaviour, personality, development and social influence
Clinical mental health, psychopathology, health, stress, assessment and treatment
Brain, cognition, biological psychology and neuropsychology
Psychological research, statistics, test theory, data science and professional ethics
adjacent: Clinical, medical, health and lifespan psychology
Social, forensic, economic, work and organisational applications of psychology
Quantitative, qualitative and evidence-based psychological research
questions: How do biological, cognitive, social and developmental processes shape behaviour?
How are psychological problems, stress and illness assessed, explained and treated?
How can psychological claims and interventions be tested with sound evidence and data?

alternatives.label: Broad psychology, behaviour & research
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum spans social, cognitive, biological, clinical, health and developmental psychology with quantitative and qualitative research methods.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Tilburg Psychology: a broad study of mind and behaviour integrating biological, cognitive, social, developmental, health and clinical psychology with research design, statistics and qualitative inquiry.
progression: Biological, behavioural, social and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, health, abnormal and developmental psychology, an advanced research seminar, psychodiagnostics and higher-level interdisciplinary study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; twelve 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Clinical, health & lifespan psychology
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres psychological problems, health, development, assessment and intervention while retaining biological, social and research foundations.
alternatives.concept: A clinical-and-health direction examining psychopathology, health, development across the lifespan, diagnosis, psychotherapy and resilience alongside epidemiology, physiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and psychological research.
progression: Behavioural, biological, social and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, health, psychopathology and development, followed by epidemiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, ethics and psychodiagnostics. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; twelve 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes clinical, biomedical, health and lifespan applications the organising priority. It replaces four upper-level philosophy and communication courses in the closest programme with epidemiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and ethics, differing by exactly four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Brain, cognition & behavioural science
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres neural, biological and computational mechanisms of cognition and behaviour while preserving core psychology and research training.
alternatives.concept: A brain-and-cognition direction combining neurobiology, perception, higher-order cognition and psycholinguistics with physiology, anatomy, genetics, laboratory science, data analysis and machine learning to investigate behaviour mechanistically.
progression: Brain, behaviour, life-science and social foundations precede neurobiology, molecular biology, data, statistics, health and abnormal psychology, then laboratory science, anatomy, disease, higher cognition, machine learning, genetics and advanced psychology research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes neural, biological and computational explanation the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by nine courses and 67.5 EC in each direction, and from the clinical route by seven courses and 52.5 EC in each direction.

notes.text: Tilburg provides a prescribed Psychology foundation followed by a dedicated major, professional skills, test theory, multiple research-methods courses, applied statistics and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can assemble substantial broad, clinical/health and brain/cognition programmes, but it does not reproduce Tilburg’s complete psychometric, professional-practice and major sequence; the 30-ECTS mobility window remains open.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates broad psychology, personality, development, social influence, research, data science and methods. Clinical/health/lifespan and brain/cognition form two further evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions, each exceeding the 30-ECTS distinctness floor. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum; the further coherent forensic, economic and work/organisational directions are recorded but cannot be constructed within that limit.
